Clidinium Bromide: A synthetic quaternary antimuscarinic; best known in fixed combination with chlordiazepoxide for IBS and peptic ulcer. First approval/introduction: Introduced 1961 (Hoffmann-La Roche); US combination with chlordiazepoxide approved 1961. Chlordiazepoxide: The first benzodiazepine, discovered by chance by Leo Sternbach at Roche in 1955. First approval/introduction: Patented 1958; approved 1960 (Hoffmann-La Roche). Dicyclomine Hydrochloride: One of the most widely used anticholinergic antispasmodics for IBS and infant colic (no longer recommended under 6 months). First approval/introduction: Synthesised c.1945 (William S. Merrell Company); marketed 1952; INN dicycloverine.
Clidinium bromide 2.5 mg + Chlordiazepoxide 5 mg + Dicyclomine 10 mg
Dual anticholinergic antispasmodic action (clidinium and dicyclomine) plus anxiolysis (chlordiazepoxide) for stress-related bowel spasm.

Clidinium Bromide Peripheral antimuscarinic agent that reduces GI motility and secretions; quaternary structure limits CNS penetration. Receptor / target profile: Peripheral muscarinic antagonist (M3-preferring); poor CNS penetration.

Chlordiazepoxide Enhances GABA-A mediated inhibition in the limbic system, reducing anxiety and associated autonomic/visceral symptoms. Receptor / target profile: Acts on benzodiazepine allosteric sites of GABA-A receptors, producing anxiolytic, sedative, anticonvulsant and muscle-relaxant effects.

Dicyclomine Hydrochloride Antimuscarinic action plus direct smooth-muscle relaxant effect, relieving GI and biliary colic and spasm. Receptor / target profile: Antimuscarinic (relatively M1-selective) plus direct smooth-muscle relaxant activity.
Summary: Incompletely absorbed (quaternary ammonium); excreted in urine and faeces.
Hepatic – to desmethylchlordiazepoxide, demoxepam, desmethyldiazepam, oxazepam
Summary: Well absorbed; Tmax 0.5–4 h. ~96% protein bound. Metabolised to active desmethylchlordiazepoxide, demoxepam and desmethyldiazepam. Half-life 5–30 h (active metabolites much longer).
Summary: Rapidly absorbed; Tmax 1–1.5 h. Half-life ~1.8 h (initial). Excreted mainly in urine.

Clidinium Bromide: Anticholinergic toxicity; supportive care. Chlordiazepoxide: Somnolence, confusion, respiratory depression, coma. Supportive care; flumazenil with caution. Dicyclomine Hydrochloride: Anticholinergic toxicity – dry hot skin, dilated pupils, tachycardia, delirium. Supportive care.
Evidence derives mainly from component and older trials of clidinium–chlordiazepoxide in IBS.
May cause dry mouth and blurred vision
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
